name: Basketball explosions
goalName: Creating an explosion effect to destroy basketballs
goal: With the new arcade machine model, it is possible for basketballs to be visible and motionless at the end of the round. There needs to be a way to destroy the balls without them just popping out of existence.

approach.text: By playing around with the particle system already added to the basketballs, I discovered the burst option in the emission. This turned out not to be the most suitable option, as it needed the emission to be turned on, leaving a trail instead.

I looked up how to create particles on runtime, and found out it can be done using "particleSystem.Emit" from <<source Setting particle burst on runtime - Unity Answers. (11-05-2016). https://answers.unity.com/questions/1184980/setting-particle-burst-on-runtime.html>>. Unfortunately, this solution did not work immediately, as it was deprecated.

Having discovered the particle system component has methods itself, I looked at what was available and came up with the following solution:<<image 7.png>>This initially did not work either, though it was visible while testing out the settings in the editor. By waiting a few seconds after the particles were emitted, the gameobject could be destroyed without it looking cut off.

normalLearnings: I learned that emitted particles are destroyed instantly when the gameobject is destroyed.
I learned that the particle system has modules to separate responsibility.
result: Once the round ends, the remaining basketballs are destroyed one by one, each creating an 'explosion' of particles as seen here:<<video https://www.youtube.com/embed/kmGLeNAJWYo>>
validation: My supervisors were satisfied with the result for now. When there is time left, it can be improved with the help of the experts at the company.
contribution: The explosions add to the game feel of the game.
